**Triage** — graded `p3`, `finding` cleared, `tests`, `pm:queue`, routed `domain:cli` (`packages/rest` is that lane).

## Confirmed at `origin/main` `2aa8456`

`handleApprovalError` has moved to `:11557` (you read "around `:11477`"). The row is there, fifth in the table:

```ts
[/^FORBIDDEN/, 403, 'FORBIDDEN'],
```

and `git show origin/main:packages/rest/src/rest-approvals-wire-codes.test.ts | grep -c "FORBIDDEN\|403"` returns **0**. The gap is exactly as filed: `THROTTLED`, `READ_BACK_FAILED` and the template-generated `APPROVAL_*_FAILED` rows are pinned live through the real routes; the row every authorisation refusal rides is not.

## ⭐ One measurement you did not make, and it is the reason this stays `p3`

I traced what happens if the row is lost. `handleApprovalError` returns `false` on no match, and both call sites are:

```ts
if (handleApprovalError(res, err)) return;
throw err;
```

with the outer catch answering `res.status(500).json({ code: 'APPROVAL_RECALL_FAILED', ... })`. So a dropped or mis-anchored `FORBIDDEN` row **fails closed** — the caller is still refused, at 500 instead of 403. There is no shape of this regression that admits an unauthorised actor.

That settles the grade. A coverage gap on a security-relevant envelope whose failure mode is fail-open would be `p2` or higher; one that can only degrade a 403 into a 500 is a contract regression, not a security one. Your own classification ("an observation and not a defect") was right, and now it has the mechanism behind it rather than the absence of a symptom.

Worth adding to the eventual test's rationale: in that degraded shape the 500 arm answers `String(error?.message ?? error).slice(0, 500)` — the **raw** `FORBIDDEN: …` message with no prefix strip. So the regression would also break the `[#13095]` anchored-strip contract, not just the status. Two contract properties ride this one row.

## Scope ruled

One `it()` in `rest-approvals-wire-codes.test.ts` (#8885), the shape you specify: through the real recall route, fake service throwing `FORBIDDEN: …`, asserting `status === 403`, `body.code === 'FORBIDDEN'`, and that the prefix is stripped from `body.error`. That third assertion is the one that would catch a regression in the anchored strip as well as in the row, so ⛔ do not drop it as redundant.

⛔ Do not add a case per refusing operation. Every authorisation refusal rides one row; pinning it once through one route is the point. A test per operation pins the routes, which the other four files already do.

⛔ Do not extend the mapping table or change any row. This card adds a pin to existing behaviour and nothing else.

⛔ Do not re-open #12775. `packages/rest` was outside its claimed file surface, which is why this is a separate card rather than an amendment — the right call.
